summary.intent: Run GSD's /gsd-plan-phase and /gsd-execute-phase workflows end-to-end for cipher-box phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust port with grant-root awareness), producing executable PLAN.md files with integrated research/verification, then auto-advancing into wave-based parallel execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed all 14 (later 16) plans with research/validation/pattern-mapping and a plan-checker pass; execution merged 11 plans (69-01 through 69-08, 69-11, 69-12, 69-15) covering the full crates/core + crates/sdk foundation (Node codec, AAD seal, gated read chain, resumable rotation engine, write-body codec). Execution twice hit architectural scope blockers on the FUSE read/write cutover (69-09) — the write-plane emit API and read adapter didn't exist — leading to two rounds of stop-and-replan; the user chose to expand the phase with new infra plans (69-15/69-16) before retrying the atomic cutover, and WinFsp/Windows work (69-14) is deferred to the user's Windows machine.

repo: GSD's commit helper reports a false-negative 'commit_failed' even when the commit succeeds cleanly (lint-staged completes fine) — always verify via `git log` before retrying.

gsd-planner writes internal pseudo-IDs (e.g. SC-01..SC-06) into a plan's `requirements:` frontmatter instead of the real roadmap requirement ID (e.g. TEST-03) — must be manually reconciled for the §13 coverage gate to pass.

API-SURFACE regen (intel hook) is TS/JS-focused and returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` on Rust-only phases — expected, not a failure; omit from planner prompts in favor of RESEARCH.md symbol locations.

Fresh git worktrees have no `node_modules`, so the husky pre-commit hook fails on first commit (`lint-staged` not found) — requires `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` inside the worktree before retrying.

`cargo fmt` run at the crate root reformats unrelated files as a side effect — executors must `git status --short` scope-check and revert stray formatting before every commit (recurred in 69-08 and 69-15).

A worktree agent's self-reported `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` can be a mis-capture (its own docs commit instead of the true fork point) — verify the actual fork base via `git merge-base` before recording/merging.

crates/fuse's write path (mkdir/upload/delete/rename) still emits legacy ECIES-wrapped FolderMetadata/FileMetadata; there is no Node write-plane emit API (`build_node`/`create_node`/`publish_node`) anywhere in crates/core or crates/sdk.
crates/fuse never references crates/sdk::listing (the gated `list_folder` read chain) — it does raw IPNS resolves directly via cipherbox_api_client at ~10 call sites.
crates/sdk/src/queue.rs's `JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` welds the write-ahead journal to the legacy type — a coupling missed by the original phase 69 plans.
PublishedNode.write_sealed existed in the schema but was never populated — seal_node only sealed the read-body; seal_published_node was added to seal both.

code.finding: rotate_one takes parent_read_key: &[u8] as a borrow, so the type system (not just convention) prevents zeroing the caller's buffer, enforcing the terminal-owner zeroization invariant.
Write path (mkdir/upload/delete/rename) emits legacy cipherbox_core::folder::FolderMetadata/FileMetadata with ECIES-wrapped keys — never migrated to Node v3.
1,958-line JournalOp structure whose parent_metadata field is typed as the legacy FolderMetadata, an unscoped coupling discovered during execution.
seal_published_node added to seal both read-body and write-body (previously only read-body was sealed via seal_node).

workflow: GSD plan:pre hooks (intel, research, pattern-mapper, schema-gate, tdd, drift) are conditionally active per phase config — frontend:false phases skip UI/security gates automatically.
The Nyquist validation gate requires the researcher to emit a '## Validation Architecture' section in RESEARCH.md before VALIDATION.md can be materialized.

Running a synchronous 'canary' plan first (before fanning out parallel worktree waves) validates the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline cheaply before committing to unattended parallel execution.

Claude Code's isolation='worktree' forks a worktree-agent-* branch from HEAD; the executor's <worktree_branch_check> guard verifies it and reports <worktree_metadata> back to the orchestrator for merge-back.

Executors following deviation 'Rule 4' correctly halt and report rather than attempting a destructive/unsafe rewrite when they discover the plan's scope assumptions don't hold (e.g. 69-09 stopping twice rather than guessing).
For a long pause (e.g. scheduled resume hours later), writing a durable handoff file to the scratchpad plus ScheduleWakeup protects against context summarization losing recovery state.

friction: The gsd-planner subagent crashed with an API error (connection closed mid-response) while writing the final plan of a 14-plan set, requiring manual disk-state diagnosis and a resumed single-plan planner run.
GSD's commit helper false-positives 'commit_failed' repeatedly, forcing manual git log verification after nearly every commit step.

Original phase 69 plans significantly underestimated the FUSE cutover: two successive in-execution architectural discoveries (no write-plane API exists; read path isn't wired to the gated listing) forced two rounds of stop/research/replan mid-execution.

A large atomic 22-file cutover plan (69-09) turned out not to be a 'mechanical flip' as designed — the infrastructure it was meant to consume (Node write-plane emit API, NodeFetcher adapter) simply didn't exist, wasting an opus executor run before the gap was caught.
